questions.text: An IP router with a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of 1500 bytes has received an IP packet of size 4404 bytes with an IP header of length 20 bytes. The values of the relevant fields in the header of the third IP fragment generated by the router for this packet are
questions.solution:
Data = 4404 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 4384 B. Max data per fragment = 1480 B (multiple of 8).

- Fragment 1: 1480 B, offset 0
- Fragment 2: 1480 B, offset 185
- Fragment 3: 4384 [latex]-[/latex] 2960 = 1424 B, offset 2960 / 8 = 370, last fragment so MF = 0

Datagram length = 1424 + 20 = 1444

Answer: MF bit: 0, Datagram Length: 1444, Offset: 370

questions.text: Every host in an IPv4 network has a 1-second resolution real-time clock with battery backup. Each host needs to generate up to 1000 unique identifiers per second. Assume that each host has a globally unique IPv4 address. Design a 50-bit globally unique ID for this purpose. After what period (in seconds) will the identifiers generated by a host wrap around?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- IPv4 address (global uniqueness): 32 bits
- Up to 1000 IDs per second: 10 bits ([latex]2^{10}=1024[/latex])
- Remaining for the clock: 50 [latex]-[/latex] 32 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 8 bits

The clock part repeats after [latex]2^8=256[/latex] seconds.

Answer: 256

questions.text:
An IP router implementing Classless Inter-domain routing (CIDR) receives a packet with address 131.23.151.76. The router's routing table has the following entries:

The identifier of the output interface on which this packet will be forwarded is _____.
questions.solution:
Address 131.23.151.76, second octet 23 = 00010111.

- 131.16.0.0/12: 16 = 0001 0000 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] first 4 bits 0001 match
- 131.28.0.0/14: 28 = 000111 00 vs 000101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no
- 131.19.0.0/16: 19 [latex]\ne[/latex] 23 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no
- 131.22.0.0/15: 22 = 0001011 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] first 7 bits 0001011 match

Longest prefix match is /15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] interface 1.

Answer: 1

questions.text:
Host A (on TCP/IP v4 network A) sends an IP datagram D to host B (also on TCP/IP V4 network B). Assume that no error occurred during the transmission of D. When D reaches B, which of the following IP header field(s) may be different from that of the original datagram D?
(i) TTL
(ii) Checksum
(iii) Fragment Offset
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- TTL is decremented at each router.
- Checksum is recomputed whenever the header changes.
- If a router fragments D, the fragments have new Fragment Offset values.

All three may differ.

Answer: (i), (ii) and (iii)

questions.text: A bit-stuffing based framing protocol uses an 8-bit delimiter pattern of 01111110. If the output bit-string after stuffing is 01111100101, then the input bit-string is
questions.solution:
The sender inserts a 0 after every five consecutive 1s. Remove it:

0 11111 0 0101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0 11111 0101 = 0111110101

Answer: 0111110101
